doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Growing up in Endicott and learning drums
title: Al Hamme and Stanley Kay as mentors
summary: Al Hamme put her in his Binghamton bands and introduced her to Slam Stewart; Stanley Kay, Buddy Rich's manager, opened her eyes in New York and is her business partner.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Is there a teacher along the way that you credit with really helping you along this path?
In Binghamton, which we were talking about before, just the area itself, there was a guy named Al Hamme who ran a lot of the jazz bands up there.
Right, I was going to ask about that.

First I started in college at SUNY Binghamton, the state university — I started at Ithaca then I finished at SUNY and Al liked the way I played and subsequently I went into all of his bands, and he booked a lot of the shows in Binghamton and I played all the time there. It was like the best possible way to train to do anything in music was to be playing in his big bands and his small bands and he introduced me to Slam Stewart and I played with Slam a lot and got to play on Slam’s last album with him, and Al introduced me to a lot of people and gave me unbelievable amounts of opportunity. Every Ice Capades that © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

came through town, every show, I played percussion for all of them. So it was phenomenal. So that was that phase of my life. But really somebody who opened my eyes unbelievably to music was Stanley Kay when I came to New York in 1986. I met him a few years later and he’s like to me a genius and so inspirational to me, not just about music, but the music business, about drumming, about jazz, about big band playing.

Yeah because he was the drummer with Josephine Baker, Patti Page and Frankie Laine and of course Buddy Rich’s assistant drummer and he managed the Buddy Rich band for 30 years. So it’s ironic that my business partner and my best friend, Stanley, was probably with Buddy in Binghamton when I was eleven.
Like watching it. And not realizing that there was this silly girl like staring in awe.
